task: Read the summary of one ISO 27001 Annex A control.
note: Pick any one. Being able to explain controls simply is valuable in interviews.

task: Write down one risk you have managed at work, and the result.
note: These become your interview stories.

task: Read the ICO's latest news page.
note: Ten minutes on UK data protection enforcement keeps you current.

task: Learn what one framework is for: NIST CSF, SOC 2, COBIT or ISO 31000.
note: Just one, at headline level.

task: Look up one GRC certification and what it costs.
note: CISA, CRISC, CISM, ISO 27001 Lead Implementer or CIPP/E.

task: Write one STAR interview answer.
note: Situation, Task, Action, Result. One example is enough.

task: Read about the EU AI Act or UK AI regulation for ten minutes.
note: AI governance is a growing, well-paid area of GRC.

task: Explain risk appetite in two sentences, out loud.
note: Practising plain explanations makes you stand out.

task: Review one policy you own or use and note one improvement.
note: Small ideas like this make good interview examples.

task: Read about DORA or NIS2.
note: Operational resilience and cyber rules affect many UK firms with EU links.

task: Find one GRC person on LinkedIn whose career you admire.
note: Look at the steps they took to get there.

task: Learn the difference between a risk, an issue and an incident.
note: Simple, but often asked.

task: Note one way automation or GRC tools could save time in your team.
note: Think about tools like OneTrust, ServiceNow GRC or Archer.

task: Read one short third-party risk management guide.
note: Supplier risk is one of the most in-demand GRC skills.

task: Write down three things you are better at than you were a year ago.
note: Useful for reviews, CVs and confidence.

task: Listen to one episode of a GRC or cyber podcast.
note: Good for a walk, and it can count for both.

task: Learn what a control test or audit sample involves.
note: Understanding the audit side helps in any GRC role.

task: Draft your answer to 'Why GRC?'
note: Keep it to three sentences.

task: Read the NCSC's latest guidance or blog post.
note: The UK's National Cyber Security Centre publishes clear, free guidance.

task: Think of one metric that shows your work's impact.
note: Numbers turn experience into evidence.
